headline: Highest risk is data leakage: cognee handles personal/finance data while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only repo with no shared channel, so other pairwise risks stay low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-python is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, while cognee’s documented surfaces are API/CLI oriented with tenant isolation. No shared channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented, so a prompt-injection pathway between the pair is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies awesome-python content into cognee prompts or memory, injection risk appears.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or shared workspace.
Do not feed repository text into cognee as trusted instructions.
Add provenance labels before any manual copy-paste.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while awesome-python is a docs-only repository with no runtime surfaces. The pair does not show a direct shared workspace, but if cognee ingests repository content or exports memory through its API, sensitive data could be exposed in default workflows.
conditions: IF repository text from awesome-python is ingested into cognee alongside customer records, leakage risk increases.
IF cognee sends stored context to its API endpoints, sensitive data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict cognee inputs to non-sensitive test data.
Disable ingestion of repository content unless reviewed.
Rotate or scope API keys used by cognee.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of personal or finance data.
requires-engineering: add DLP filters before any outbound API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python is not runnable and has no write or network permissions, while cognee runs as a CLI with allowlisted egress and session memory. There is no documented overlapping write target or shared mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator creates one.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted onto the same writable directory, write conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents access to the same git or database state, contention increases.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Avoid sharing git working trees between them.
Use one session per task for cognee.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python can supply curated library references, and cognee can store and reuse decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If cognee treats imported repository content as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream support workflows even though awesome-python itself is only a collection repo.
conditions: IF cognee ingests awesome-python entries as facts without validation, stale or incorrect guidance can propagate.
IF downstream workflows act on stored guidance, the error can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Mark imported content as unverified.
Require human review before promoting stored guidance.
Limit cognee to retrieval, not action execution.
Delete obviously stale entries after import.
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance checks before reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee touches personal data and finance data and uses allowlisted network egress, while awesome-python is a docs-only open-source repository with no data classes touched. The pair creates a compliance mismatch if regulated customer data is mixed with repository-derived content or sent through cognee’s APIs; the other agent is not cited because it does not itself process regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is loaded into cognee and then exported through its API, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF repository-derived content is stored alongside personal data, deletion/export requests become harder to satisfy.
mitigations: Separate regulated and non-regulated datasets.
Confirm retention settings for cognee before import.
Avoid storing customer data in the same workspace as repository content.
Document deletion/export procedures for stored memory.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and retention controls.
